evidence_assessments.rationale: Corroborates that Vo Nguyen Giap was promoted directly to Senior General (Đại tướng) by President Ho Chi Minh at the age of 37 without going through intermediate ranks.
Confirms Vo Nguyen Giap did not go through intermediate military ranks and became the first Senior General of the Vietnam People's Army at age 37.
Corroborates the promotion at age 37 by Ho Chi Minh and references his role as Commander-in-Chief (Tổng Tư lệnh).
Shows a quote by Tran Van Tra mentioning General Vo Nguyen Giap's leadership, but does not verify whether he was the sole Commander-in-Chief.

value.rationale: The retrieved external evidence completely verifies that General Vo Nguyen Giap was promoted directly to the rank of Đại tướng (Senior General) by President Ho Chi Minh at the age of 37 without passing through intermediate ranks. However, none of the retrieved sources definitively prove the material claim that he was the 'only' (duy nhất) Commander-in-Chief (Tổng Tư lệnh) of the Vietnam People's Army.
value.uncertainty: Lack of explicit historical evidence confirming or refuting whether Vo Nguyen Giap is the sole person ever to hold the title of Tổng Tư lệnh of the Vietnam People's Army.
limitations: Retrieved text snippets only confirm his promotion and mention his role as Commander-in-Chief, but do not address whether any other person held the position of Tổng Tư lệnh.
